1  Safety
1.1  Intended use
The HX-400 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump for clean and lightly contaminated liquids.
It is designed for continuous duty in industrial process service: cooling water, condensate, process
water, light hydrocarbons and, in the duplex variant, chloride-bearing media.
The pump is not suitable for liquids containing abrasive solids above 50 mg/l, for slurries, for media
that gas off inside the casing, or for service above the temperature limits in section 12.2. Using it
outside these limits voids the warranty and may cause the seal to fail without warning.
 DANGER
Never run the pump against a closed discharge valve for longer than 60 seconds. The
liquid in the casing heats rapidly and the casing may rupture. The temperature rise at
zero flow is about

charge valve for longer than 60 seconds. The
liquid in the casing heats rapidly and the casing may rupture. The temperature rise at
zero flow is about 9 kelvin per minute for the HX-400.
1.2  Qualification of personnel
Installation, commissioning and maintenance may be carried out only by people who are trained for
the work and who have read this manual. Electrical work is reserved for qualified electricians. Work
on pumps that have carried hazardous media additionally requires the permit described in the
operator's own procedure.

1.3  Residual risks
Even when the pump is installed and operated correctly, the following risks remain and must be
managed by the operating company:
  Hot

esidual risks
Even when the pump is installed and operated correctly, the following risks remain and must be
managed by the operating company:
  Hot surfaces. The casing and the bearing housing reach the temperature of the pumped liquid.
Above 60 C the surfaces must be guarded or marked.
  Rotating parts. The coupling guard must be in place before the motor is energised. The guard is
part of the CE conformity of the unit.

  Stored pressure. The casing holds pressure after the pump stops. Vent through the casing vent
before loosening any joint.
  Residual liquid. The casing drains incompletely; about 4 litres remain in the volute of an HX-400
after the drain plug is opened.
  Noise. Sound pressure at one metre is 78 dB(A) at the duty point and rises toward the end of the
curve. Hearing protection is required above 80 dB(A).
  Electrostatic charge. When pumping non-conductive liquids the casing must be bonded to the
plant earth.

2  Transport and storage
2.1  Lifting
The bare pump weighs 410 kg; the pump on its baseplate with motor weighs between 980 and 1140
kg depending on the motor frame. The weight is stamped on the nameplate and on the shipping
crate.
 DANGER
Lift the assembled unit by the four baseplate lifting points only. Lifting by the pump
eyebolt alone will tip the unit: the eyebolt is rated for the bare pump. Never lift by the
motor eyebolt when the motor is bolted to the baseplate.

4.2  Construction
The HX-400 is a back pull-out design. The bearing housing, shaft, impeller and seal come out of the
casing as one assembly once the coupling spacer and the casing bolts are removed; the casing stay

ng housing, shaft, impeller and seal come out of the
casing as one assembly once the coupling spacer and the casing bolts are removed; the casing stays
bolted to the pipework. This is the reason the casing bolt torque in section 5.7 matters so much: those
bolts are disturbed at every overhaul.
The rotor runs in two bearings. The drive end carries a 6309 C3 deep groove ball bearing taking
radial load; the non-drive end carries a 3309 C3 double row angular contact bearing taking the
hydraulic axial thrust. Both are oil lubricated from the common sump in the bearing housing.
Axial thrust is balanced by back vanes on the impeller shroud rather than by balance holes. Back
vanes also keep solids out of the seal chamber, which is why the seal faces last longer on this design
than on the supersede

vanes also keep solids out of the seal chamber, which is why the seal faces last longer on this design
than on the superseded HX-380.

5  Installation
5.1  Location
Allow 800 mm clear in front of the bearing housing for back pull-out, and 600 mm above the unit for
lifting. A pump that cannot be pulled out without dismantling pipework will not be maintained properly,
whatever the maintenance schedule says.
The foundation must be able to carry three times the static weight of the unit and must be isolated
from the building structure where vibration transmission matters.

the foundation bolts to their final torque until the grout has cured for the time the grout manufacturer
states, typically sev

5.5  Flange bolting - general
Flange joints are tightened in a crosswise pattern in at least three passes: 30% of final torque, 70%,
then 100%. A fourth pass at 100% in a clockwise sequence confirms that no bolt has relaxed.
Re-check the torque after the first thermal cycle and again after 24 hours of operation on services
above 100 C.
All torque figures in this manual are for lubricated threads and bolt faces, using a molybdenum
disulphide paste or an equivalent anti-seize with a friction coefficient of 0.12. If the threads are dry,

8.3  Minimum flow and recirculation
Minimum continuous flow for the HX-400 is 15 per cent of the best efficiency flow, that is 36 m3/h at
the 385 mm trim. Below this figure the liquid recirculates inside the impeller eye, which raises the
temperature in the casing and loads the bearings unevenly. Revision R5 of this manual raised the
figure from 10 per cent after repeated recirculation damage in t

in the casing and loads the bearings unevenly. Revision R5 of this manual raised the
figure from 10 per cent after repeated recirculation damage in the field.
Where the process can call for less than minimum flow, fit an automatic recirculation valve returning
to the suction vessel, not to the suction line: returning hot liquid directly to the suction line reduces the
available NPSH and causes cavitation.

11.3  Reassembly
Reassembly is the reverse of dismantling, with the following points that are specific to this frame:
  Heat bearings to 110 C in an induction heater and slide them on. Never drive a bearing on, and
never heat above 125 C.
  The angular contact pair at the non-drive end is fitted back to back. Fitted the wrong way round, the
pump will run but the bearings fail within a few hundred hours.
  Fit a new shaft sleeve O-ring and lubricate it with the pumped liquid, not with grease. Mineral
grease swells FKM.
  The impeller nut is tightened anti-clockwise to 120 Nm. Lock it with the tab wa

with the pumped liquid, not with grease. Mineral
grease swells FKM.
  The impeller nut is tightened anti-clockwise to 120 Nm. Lock it with the tab washer; the tab washer
is a single-use part.
  Set the axial position of the rotor before the casing goes back on: impeller front face to casing 1.8 to
2.2 mm, adjusted at the bearing housing shims.
  Fit a new casing gasket dry. Do not use jointing compound; it prevents the correct gasket stress
from developing.
  Tighten the casing bolts crosswise in three passes to 210 Nm.
  Fill with 0.90 litre of Halstrom HLP-46 before turning the shaft under power.
  Re-align after the casing is bolted back to the pipework, not before.

nameplate is removed and destroyed so that the machine cannot be re-sold with its certification.
All addresses in this manual are fictional and belong to a fictional company. This document was written as training and
assessment material.

1  Purpose and scope
This document does two things. Sections 1 to 5 set out how Rendell manages safety on the work we
do: who is responsible for what, how a job is assessed before it starts, and what protective equipment
is required. Sections 6 to 9 are the substance register: a condensed data sheet for each hazardous
substance we hold.
The procedures here apply alongside the client's own rules. Where the two differ, the stricter rule
applies. Where a client rule would require us to work less safely than this document, the work stops
and the supervisor is called.

THIS PROCEDURE SAVES LIVES
Three of the four fatal accidents in Dutch industrial maintenance that the sector body
reviewed in its last report involved equipment that was believed to be isolated and was
not. Every step in section 5 exists because somebody was killed when it was skipped.
not. Every step in section 5 exists because somebody was killed when it was skipped.

1  Purpose and scope
This procedure sets out how Rendell makes plant safe to work on and how it controls entry into
confined spaces. It applies to all work on client plant, in the Rendell workshop, and to subcontractors
working under a Rendell order.
Most client sites operate their own permit system. Where they do, that system governs and this
procedure describes how Rendell staff work within it. Where a client has no system, or where the
work is in the Rendell workshop, this procedure is the system.
 THE RULE THAT OVERRIDES EVERYTHING ELSE
If you did not isolate it yourself, or you did not see it isolated and prove it dead
yourself, it is live. There is no exception to this for experience, for seniority, for time
pressure, or for an assurance given over the radio.

Isolation
Positive separation of the equipment from every source of energy, so that the energy
cannot be restored accidentally.
Positive isolation
A physical break: a removed spool piece, a spade or blind, or a disconnected and
withdrawn electrical circuit. A closed valve alone is not positive isolation.
Lock-out
A personal padlock applied to an isolating device so that it cannot be operated. One
lock, one key, one person.
Tag-out

Where more than two people work on the same isolation, use a lock box. The isolating authority
applies the isolations, puts the keys in the box and locks it. Every person working on the equipment

is removed, which means the equipment cannot be re-energised while anybody is still working.

6  Confined spaces
6.1  What counts
A confined space is not only a tank. The test is whether the space is enclosed enough for the
atmosphere to go wrong, or for a person to be hard to get out. The following are treated as confined
spaces at Rendell:
  Process vessels, tanks, silos and columns.
  Pump pits and sumps deeper than 1.2 metres.
  Valve chambers and inspection pits.
  Culverts, sewers and interceptors.
  Large bore pipework a person can enter.
  Heat exchanger shells and water boxes.
  Trenches deeper than 1.2 metres where gas may collect.
  The inside of a drained cooling tower basin with the fan stopped.
  Any space the client has designated as a confined space.
 A space becomes confined because of what is happening in it, not only because of its shape. An
open-topped

lient has designated as a confined space.
 A space becomes confined because of what is happening in it, not only because of its shape. An
open-topped pit is confined while solvent cleaning is going on inside it, even though it is open to

6.6  Stopping an entry
The entry stops and everybody comes out immediately if any of the following happens. There is no
assessment to make and no permission to seek.
  Any gas reading moves outside the limits of table 6.1.
  A gas detector alarms, whatever the reading afterwards.
  Communication with the standby person is lost.
  Ventilation stops.
  Lighting fails.
  An entrant feels unwell, dizzy, or reports a headache.
  The site alarm sounds.
  The permit expires and has not been extended.
  Anybody, inside or outside, calls for evacuation.

Dit voorschrift beschrijft wat er aan een pompinstallatie gebeurt, hoe vaak, en waaraan het
resultaat moet voldoen. Waar dit voorschrift en de handleiding van de fabrikant van elkaar afwijken,

1  Doel en toepassingsgebied
Dit voorschrift legt het preventieve onderhoud aan pompinstallaties vast. Het doel is drieledig: de
installaties beschikbaar houden, de kosten van storingen beperken, en kunnen aantonen dat het
onderhoud is uitgevoerd zoals de fabrikant en de wetgever dat verlangen.
Het voorschrift geldt voor alle pompinstallaties van de HX-serie die Rendell in beheer heeft, zowel op
eigen locatie als bij opdrachtgevers waar Rendell het onderhoud contractueel verzorgt. Voor pompen
van een ander merk geldt OV-221.
Correctief onderhoud, dus herstel na een storing, valt buiten dit voorschrift en is beschreven in
OV-230.
